newsitem.title: USA: FBI probes funds charge against Burton - report.
newsitem.headline: FBI probes funds charge against Burton - report.

text.p: The FBI has begun a preliminary inquiry into allegations that Republican Representative Dan Burton of Indiana threatened a lobbyist with loss of work last year if he did not raise funds for Burton's campaign, the Washington Post reported Saturday.

An FBI agent had scheduled an interview next week with Mark Siegel, a former lobbyist for the Pakistani government, who alleged in a memo that he was "shaken down" by Burton, the newspaper said, quoting Siegel's lawyer.

Siegel's accusations, which Burton has denied, were reported in the Post Wednesday. The lobbyist for the government of former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said he was approached by Burton early last year to raise "at least $5,000" for his re-election campaign.

When he was unable to do so, Siegel said, the congressman complained to the then-ambassador for Pakistan in Washington and later threatened to make sure "none of his friends or colleagues" would meet with Siegel or his associates.
As chairman of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, Burton is leading the highly publicised investigation of alleged fund-raising abuses in last year's election campaigns.
The report of the FBI inquiry came as the House voted Friday to give Burton's committee a $3.8 million budget to probe possible Democratic fund-raising abuses.
Following the funding approval, Burton said he did not expect to begin hearings for a month or more. He also said Republican leaders supported him despite his own fund-raising controversy.
"They are all behind me 100 percent," Burton said. "I am probably going to be attacked again and again and again and again because I'm in the position I'm in."
